title: Landlord repairs
tagline: Learn to get repairs done and keep rent stable without damaging the landlord relationship.
you_are: a tenant with a maintenance issue and a rent-stability goal
setting: Conversations happen in the rental unit, the building hallway, or by phone and email follow-up, often with the landlord or their property manager.

scenarios.label: First repair request
scenarios.desc: You walk the landlord through the issue for the first time and ask for a fix.
scenarios.setup: The landlord is standing in your doorway after you texted them about a leaking bathroom pipe. They look at the stain on the ceiling and say, ‘Okay, what exactly am I looking at here?’
scenarios.skills: Clear problem description and collaborative tone
scenarios.objective: Get a concrete repair commitment with a timeline.

scenarios.label: Chasing a stalled repair
scenarios.desc: The landlord acknowledged the issue but nothing has happened for two weeks.
scenarios.setup: You catch the property manager in the laundry room. They check their phone and say, ‘Yeah, I emailed the owner about the plumber. Haven’t heard back yet.’
scenarios.objective: Secure a specific date for the repair visit.
scenarios.moment: Saturday 10:00 am, washer spin cycle humming

scenarios.label: Negotiating rent stability
scenarios.desc: The landlord hints at a rent increase at renewal while the repair is still open.
scenarios.setup: You sit across from the landlord at a cafe near the building. They slide a renewal letter toward you and say, ‘Market rents have gone up quite a bit. This number reflects that.’
scenarios.skills: Leveraging repair history and lease terms for rent stability
scenarios.objective: Agree on a renewal rate at or near current rent with the repair completed.

buyers.angle: Easy because she values clear written proof.
Hard because he wants quick cash flow.
Hard because she distrusts rent promises.
Hard because he enforces strict lease terms.
Easy because she enjoys helping tenants.

objections: I can’t stall repairs for another month
Your lease allows rent increases with thirty days notice
I need proof the leak was caused by your negligence
The building’s roof is new and under warranty
You haven’t paid rent on time in the past
I’ve already spoken with the housing authority
The cost of repairs exceeds my yearly budget
I’m not obligated to waive any fees

rubric.label: Issue clarity
rubric.what: You describe the problem, its impact, and the exact fix needed in specific, factual language.

rubric.label: Written follow-up
rubric.what: You confirm every verbal agreement with a dated email or message that summarises the commitment.

rubric.label: Lease knowledge
rubric.what: You reference the correct lease clauses, habitability standards, and notice periods without guessing.

rubric.label: Timeline accountability
rubric.what: You pin the landlord to a concrete date or milestone and confirm what happens if it slips.

rubric.label: Compliance honesty
rubric.what: You never withhold rent illegally, misrepresent the unit condition, or skip required notice steps.

pitfalls: Withholding rent without following the legal repair-and-deduct or escrow process for your jurisdiction.
Accepting a verbal promise without a written confirmation that includes a date.
Agreeing to a rent increase before the outstanding repair is verified complete.
line: Asking my landlord to fix a problem and hold the rent steady

research.text: To ask your landlord to fix a problem and hold the rent steady, follow up any phone conversation with a written statement—an email is sufficient. Explain yourself clearly and if you'll be late on rent, explain why. Make a list of the issues you’d like addressed to focus your conversation and resolve the situation. If the problem is severe and affects your health and safety, contact relief agencies, churches, family, friends, and neighbors for assistance in vacating. Keep a copy of your written lease and record any changes or addendums to the agreement. Keep financial records and receipts for your payments. A witness to these conversations can be helpful.
